```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(shokenuse)
```

The Overview tab answers the first question: how much did I use? It gives totals for the filtered data and a chart of each day.

## Value boxes

| Box | What it shows |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Tokens | Sum of `tokens`. Cache reads are most of this. |
| Cost (USD) | Sum of `cost`, ignoring blank costs. API list price equivalent, not a subscription bill. |
| Prompts | Number of rows (one per prompt). |
| Sessions | Number of distinct `session` ids. |
| Cost / prompt | Mean `cost` per prompt. |

## Daily usage by project

The chart stacks tokens or cost for each day by project. The switch in the card header picks the measure. The 8 projects with the most tokens get their own color; the rest are grouped as `other`.

The code below draws the same chart and returns the data behind it:

```{r}
#| label: daily
metrics <- util_read_token_metrics()
util_plot_daily(metrics, "cost")

# The data behind the chart
metrics |>
  util_lump_projects(n = 8) |>
  util_summarise_metrics(by = c("day", "project"))
```

## Call stack

The UI builds its five value boxes with the internal `.value_box()` helper, and the server draws the daily chart. The call tree below is built with [`stackcallr`](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/stackcallr/). `call_tree_dir()` parses the files in `R/` without running them, so the tree always matches the code.

```{r}
#| label: call-stack-overview
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("stackcallr", quietly = TRUE)
#| collapse: false
#| comment: ""
stackcallr::call_tree_dir("../R", root = "mod_overview_ui")
stackcallr::call_tree_dir("../R", root = "mod_overview_server", exclude = "%||%")
```
